analysis.investment_thesis: Alembic is a century-old integrated pharma stalwart with 8.6% revenue CAGR but a net profit CAGR of -2.3% over nine years — a classic case of topline growth not flowing to the bottom line. At P/E 23x with earnings actually declining, the PEG is effectively infinite, making this a terrible GARP candidate.
key_strengths: High gross margins (71.5%) reflect genuine product quality and formulation depth across 12+ therapeutic areas
Low D/E of 0.28 and 69.7% promoter holding signal management alignment and financial discipline — until 2025
Forward P/E of 18.5x implies the market expects earnings recovery, leaving some optionality
key_risks: Earnings destruction: net profit collapsed from INR 1,146 Cr (2021) to INR 582 Cr (2025) — nearly halved despite revenue growing 24%
2025 cash flow alarm: OCF cratered from INR 803 Cr to just INR 88 Cr, FCF swung to -INR 466 Cr, and borrowings tripled from INR 513 Cr to INR 1,489 Cr in a single year
Finance costs compounding at 35.9% CAGR — rising debt load eating into already-thin operating margins (11.4%)
red_flags: PEG ratio is effectively undefined/infinite — P/E of 23x against negative earnings growth (-2.3% CAGR) is the opposite of GARP
FY2025 free cash flow turned sharply negative (-INR 466 Cr) after being +INR 487 Cr in FY2024 — a dramatic single-year reversal
Borrowings spiked 190% YoY (INR 513 Cr → INR 1,489 Cr in 2025) suggesting a new heavy capex cycle before the last one paid off
EBITDA 9Y CAGR is -0.3% — a company generating less operating profit today than it did in 2016 despite 8.6% revenue growth
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Alembic fails my most basic test: the story doesn't hold up when you look at earnings. Revenue grew from INR 3,166 Cr to INR 6,672 Cr over nine years — respectable 8.6% CAGR — but net profit actually shrank from INR 720 Cr to INR 582 Cr. That means every rupee of new revenue came with deteriorating economics. The company went through a massive capex supercycle (CWIP hit INR 2,304 Cr in 2022), which I could forgive if it generated returns — but operating margins are now only 11.4% versus what would've been needed to justify the investment. With a P/E of 23x and negative earnings growth, the PEG ratio is essentially a red alarm siren.

FY2025 data raises the urgency. Operating cash flow collapsed 89% in a single year (INR 803 Cr → INR 88 Cr), free cash flow turned -INR 466 Cr, and the company raised borrowings from INR 513 Cr to INR 1,489 Cr — a new capex wave before proving returns on the last one. ROE at 11.4% sits below my 12% floor. This is a stalwart that has become a capital-intensive treadmill. I'd rather own a fast grower compounding earnings at 25% than this. Pass.
